topic: Word Usage (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)

sections.title: Advanced Concept of Word Usage
sections.content: In Level 2, words are sometimes used in ways that differ from their most common meanings. Many words can function as both nouns and verbs, and their meanings change depending on the context. Questions often include usages that sound correct but are actually incorrect collocations.

sections.title: Words Used in Unfamiliar Ways
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the common meaning of the given word. Step 2: Check whether it is used as a noun, verb, or adjective in the sentence. Step 3: Understand its less common meaning through the context. Step 4: Match it with the meaning of the sentence. Example: 'His energy began to flag after the long journey.' Here 'flag' is used as a verb meaning 'to weaken or decline.'

sections.title: Word as a Verb from a Noun
sections.content: Step 1: Identify whether a noun is being used as a verb. Step 2: Understand the contextual meaning of that verb. Step 3: Check whether the sentence meaning is logical. Example: 'The technician doctored the report.' Here 'doctor' is used as a verb meaning 'to alter or manipulate.'

sections.title: Collocation Awareness
sections.content: Step 1: Recognize words that are commonly used together. Step 2: Check whether the sentence contains a natural combination. Step 3: If the combination seems unusual, it may indicate an error. Example: 'Strong tea' is correct, while 'Powerful tea' is an incorrect collocation.

sections.title: Subtle Misuse Detection
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the meaning of the entire sentence. Step 2: Identify the grammatical role of the key word. Step 3: Check whether the word forms a correct collocation in the context. Step 4: Verify both meaning and usage. Example: 'He made a big crime.' Here 'big crime' is incorrect; the correct collocation is 'serious crime.'

sections.title: Common Confusing Word Usage
sections.content: Some words change meaning depending on context. Example: 'Book' as a noun means a written work, but as a verb it means to make a reservation. 'Address' as a noun means a location, while as a verb it means to speak about or deal with an issue.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Choosing answers based only on the most common meaning of a word. 2. Ignoring collocations. 3. Not understanding the difference between noun and verb forms. 4. Assuming a word is correct without checking the context.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2 Word Usage questions, recognizing less common meanings and correct collocations is important. First understand the sentence meaning, then identify the grammatical role of the word, and finally check whether the usage is natural and correct.

tricks.title: Context Meaning Trick
tricks.explanation: If the common meaning of a word does not fit, try understanding its meaning from the context.
tricks.example: The engine began to cough. (Here 'cough' means the engine started malfunctioning.)

tricks.title: Noun to Verb Conversion
tricks.explanation: Many nouns can be used as verbs in English.

tricks.title: Collocation Memory Trick
tricks.explanation: Some words naturally occur together in fixed combinations.

tricks.title: Meaning Logic Check
tricks.explanation: Read the sentence and check whether the word usage is logically correct.
tricks.example: He caught a cold (correct), He caught a fever (unnatural).

tricks.title: Verb Role Identification
tricks.explanation: If the word shows an action, understand it in its verb sense.

tricks.title: Replacement Trick
tricks.explanation: Replace the word with a similar meaning word to test the sentence.
tricks.example: His energy flagged → His energy decreased.

tricks.title: Common Pair Trick
tricks.explanation: Some word pairs are commonly used together.

tricks.title: Sound Correct Trap
tricks.explanation: Sometimes a sentence sounds correct but the collocation is wrong.
